leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: All, Both, Either, Neither, None
leadIn.content: Comparing items in a group: Both cars are clean, but neither car is cheap. Use these words to talk about two or more things together.

form.title: Form & Structure: All, Both, Either, Neither, None
form.content: Both / Either / Neither + singular/plural nouns or 'of' + pronouns. All / None + plural or uncountable nouns.

controlledPractice.question: Two books, both mine: '___ books are mine.'
controlledPractice.explanation: Both is used for exactly two things.

controlledPractice.question: Neither takes a ___ verb.
controlledPractice.explanation: Either and neither are followed by a singular verb, even though they refer to two things.

controlledPractice.question: A whole group with zero exceptions found: '___ of my friends were late.'
controlledPractice.explanation: None is used for groups of three or more, meaning zero.
